transcript.text: I work all the time. These are my weekly
work schedules in different seasons of
business. Number one, management
consulting job after college. I worked
9:00 to 5:00 5 days a week, and then
maybe made 50 grand a year during that
period. Number two was United Fitness,
building my first gym. I worked 14 to
16-hour days. My first session was at
4:30 in the morning. So, I had to wake
up before that to prepare the gym. Then
from 5:00 to 9:00, I did all the rest of
my classes. Then 9:00 to 11:00, I would
focus on marketing. 11:00 to 4:00, I
would take sales appointments and do the
rest of the stuff and set up for the
afternoon. 4:00 to 8:30, I would do my
evening classes. Then I did all my admin
work and did afternoon sales or evening
sales. I was making maybe $20,000 a
month. Third was GymLaunch. So, the
first phase of GymLaunch, I was on-site
launching gyms. And again, I was working
12 to 16 hours a day. I'd wake up and
immediately send my text reminders for
the morning. And then I would go
straight to the gym and set up for my
first sales of the day. All morning, I
would basically just set sales
appointments from the beginning of the
day to the end of the day. And any times
where sales appointments didn't show up,
I would check the ad performance, I
would make more ads, and I would
continue to work leads and remind people
as they continue to come in. With this
schedule, when it was just me, I was
making $100,000 a month. Over time, I
got to two or $300,000 a month with a
team. But then I transitioned to
licensing, which was yet again 12 to
14-hour days. In the morning though, I
would do deep work with whatever would
grow the business the most. In the
middle of the day, I still had sales
calls. In the afternoon, I handled all
the fulfillment and support and kind of
the building part of the business. With
this schedule, our first full 12
calendar months made $16 million in
profit. The fourth season was at
acquisition.com managing our portfolio.
Again, 12 to 14-hour days. And it had to
switch between maker and manager, and
just as maker. I either have two deep
work blocks a day, one in the morning,
one in the evening, or I have a deep
work block in the morning and then
back-to-back meetings in the evening,
which I usually just do on Mondays.
